title: Evaluator output record
description: Structured evaluator output (E-DI Contracts v1.1 s5). Structured data, never prose alone; prose may accompany it but may not replace it. Every score carries evidence: a score without evidence is discarded, not averaged. A record with ratified=false can never be part of an `accepted` terminal state.

iteration.description: Counted from 0 before the first generation, incremented once per generation. Written to the record at generation time (the worked trace in s3: generation 1 => iteration 1).

anchor_note.description: What this score means here. The evidence accompanying the score.

evidence_channel.description: Which channel produced the evidence for this dimension (s7.2).

ground_truth_access.description: Closed enum (s5). saw_gt invalidates this dimension's evidence — the channel had access to the answer it was checking — and the dimension then fails.

evidence_ref.description: Where the independent evidence lives (path, artifact id, measurement). Optional but strongly preferred: the orchestrator must be able to re-examine it without re-running the loop.

pass_rule.description: Echoed from the job packet, fixed before the run. The evaluator reports it; it does not choose it.

class.description: Violation class, so cheap defects route to automatic regeneration and consequential ones route to a person.

evidence.description: The quoted text or observed behaviour that constitutes the violation.

fix.description: The change that resolves it. Sent back to the generator as a constraint on the next iteration.

verdict.description: RECOMMENDED verdict only. s4: the evaluator emits scores, violations and a recommended verdict; it does not own the loop. The orchestrator is the sole applier of the pass rule, the cap, and escalation. s5: exactly these four values — implementations must not invent synonyms (no 'minor-revision' alongside 'regenerate').

ground_truth_ref.description: The artifact or invariant this scoring used.

evaluator_identity.description: model + version. If generator and evaluator are the same model, s4 requires that fact to be recorded with the job.

channel_blind.description: s5: asserts every evidence channel met s7.2.

ratified.description: s5: asserts no must-ask value is proposed/unratified. ratified=false can never be part of an `accepted` terminal state.

unevidenced_dimensions.description: Dimensions that could not be judged. s5: a dimension with no evidence FAILS, and a job containing one can never reach `accepted` — its exit is a forced `needs_human`, not `rejected`. Do not synthesise a below-floor score for it: that puts an invented number into min() and misreports why the job stopped.

notes.description: Prose. May accompany the structured record; may not replace it.
